# Merging the Last Two Commits in Git

You can combine your last two commits into one using **interactive rebase** or **soft reset**.

## Method 1: Interactive Rebase (Recommended)

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

In the editor that opens, you'll see something like:
```
pick abc1234 First commit message
pick def5678 Second commit message
```

Change the second `pick` to `squash` (or `s`):
```
pick abc1234 First commit message
squash def5678 Second commit message
```

Save and close. A new editor will open allowing you to edit the combined commit message. Save again to finish.

## Method 2: Soft Reset

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~2
git commit -m "New combined commit message"
```

This resets the branch pointer back 2 commits but keeps all changes staged, then creates a single new commit.

## Method 3: Reset + Amend (Quick One-Liner Style)

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git commit --amend --no-edit
```

This merges the last commit into the previous one, keeping the older commit's message.

## ⚠️ Important Warning

**Don't do this to commits you've already pushed to a shared branch.** It rewrites history. If you must, you'll need:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease
```

And coordinate with your team to avoid breaking their work.

## Which to Use?

- **Interactive rebase** — best when you want to edit the message or squash more commits
- **Soft reset** — fastest when you want a fresh combined message
- **Reset + amend** — quickest when keeping the existing message is fine
